To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AC6, but not AC5, is tightly regulated by receptor-independent intrinsic Gi activity, thus maintaining low basal cAMp levels in the functional membrane compartment regulating contractility.

the inhibitory activity of Gi upon AC6 is necessary to maintain low basal levels of cAMP in the compartment that regulates contractile function in the heart, thus providing a potential mechanism for regulating contractility.

constitutive Gi inhibition of AC6 regulates basal cAMP level in the membrane surface of cardiomyocytes and is necessary for simultaneous PDE3/PDE4 inhibition to increase in vivo and ex-vivo contractility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of cardiac contractility.
the mechanisms by which the heart adapts to physiological and pathophysiological conditions.
the role of G protein-coupled receptors in cardiac physiology and pathophysiology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AC5 and AC5KO are functionally redundant with AC6, and that AC5 and 6 have overlapping functions, but that AC6 is more important in regulating contractility.
AC5 and AC 6 have different regulatory properties in the heart.
AC5 is not involved in the regulation of cardiac contractility and that AC6 is the main isoform that is responsible for the intrinsic receptor-independent Gi inhibition of AC in the rat heart.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Gi is constitutively active in the heart and that Gi regulates AC6 activity to maintain low basal cAMP concentrations in the functional compartment of the heart that regulates contractility.
Gi is a constitutive inhibitor of AC6 and thus maintains low basal levels of cAMP at the membrane surface that regulates contractile function.
the Gi-AC6 interaction is critical for the regulation of cardiac contractility by cAMP and that this mechanism is lost in AC6 knockout mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Gi inhibitory activity is AC subtype specific, which is an important finding for future studies of cardiac physiology and pathophysiology.
AC6 is the only AC subtype that can be modulated by Gi.
AC6 is the only AC subtype that regulates contractile function through intrinsic receptor-independent Gi inhibition.
